sample.question:
Tower of Hanoi is a classic puzzle with three pegs labeled A, B and C (left to right) and several disks of different sizes. Disks are numbered by size: disk 1 is the smallest. A disk's number is printed on it. Only the TOP disk of a peg can be moved, and it may only be placed on an empty peg or on top of a LARGER disk. The move X->Y means: take the top disk of peg X and put it on peg Y.

You want to gather all 5 disks on peg C in as few moves as possible. Starting from the position in the image, which move should you make FIRST? Exactly one of the moves below starts an optimal solution.

Options:
[1] A->B
[2] A->C
[3] B->A
[4] B->C
[5] C->A
[6] C->B
sample.analysis:
Initial position: peg A: disks [4, 1] (bottom to top); peg B: disks [5, 3, 2] (bottom to top); peg C: empty. A breadth-first search shows the optimum from here is 22 moves.
Evaluate every possible first move:
A->B: legal; after it, the remaining optimum is 23 moves, total 1 + 23 = 24.
A->C: legal; after it, the remaining optimum is 23 moves, total 1 + 23 = 24.
B->A: illegal (disk 2 would land on the smaller disk 1).
B->C: legal; after it, the remaining optimum is 21 moves, total 1 + 21 = 22. <- optimal
C->A: illegal (peg C is empty).
C->B: illegal (peg C is empty).
Only B->C keeps the total at 22 moves, so it is the unique optimal first move. The option number is 4.
